interest: Shows Japan's 1923-33 child-labor reforms, with Consul Garrels detailing Tokyo's child peddlers, beggars, and geishas.
overview: This file (decimal 894.5047) covers U.S. State Department diplomatic and consular reporting from Tokyo between May 1923 and October 1933 regarding child labor and protective social legislation in Japan. The materials include a May 1923 despatch from Chargé d'Affaires Hugh R. Wilson enclosing an English translation of Law No. 23 (the 1923 amendments to the Factory Law of 1911), which raised the minimum employment age, limited hours for women and juvenile workers under sixteen, and placed restrictions on hazardous and night labor. The file concludes with an October 1933 consular report by Consul General Arthur Garrels on the enactment of the Child Welfare Law, which prohibited the exploitation of children under fourteen in begging, peddling, entertainment, and serving in drinking establishments, accompanied by statistics on affected children in Tokyo and government relief efforts for impoverished families.

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting a translation of the amended Japanese Factory Law and explaining new statutory restrictions on child labor in industrial sectors.
subfiles.summary: Wilson reports Japan's amended Factory Law bars employing minors under 15 in factories, mines, and construction, with limited exceptions.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 594 from Hugh R. Wilson on the Amended Factory Law

subfiles.about: Official English translation of Japanese Law No. 23 amending the Factory Law of 1911 regarding working hours, child labor, and workplace safety.
subfiles.summary: An official translation of Law No. 23 sanctioned on March 29, 1923, which extensively revised Japan's 1911 Factory Law. The statute restricts working hours for women and male minors under sixteen to eleven hours per day, mandates rest periods and bimonthly holidays, and prohibits night work between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. It further bans minors and female workers from cleaning or repairing machinery in motion and handling toxic or explosive substances, establishes employer liability for industrial injuries and deaths, and outlines administrative inspection and penalty procedures.
subfiles.title: Translation of Law No. 23: Law Amending the Factory Law

subfiles.about: Consular report detailing the provisions and initial enforcement of Japan's new Child Welfare Law protecting minors under fourteen from exploitation.
subfiles.summary: Garrels reports Japan's 1933 Child Welfare Law bars child beggars, peddlers, and geishas under 14, drawing on Tokyo data showing over 1,500 affected children.
subfiles.title: Report on Child Welfare Law by Arthur Garrels
